messages:
maria_support: FYI Silverpine just opened a ticket — p99 for embeddings endpoint shot from ~350ms to ~2.8s starting ~06:00 UTC. They say no change on their side.

emma_cs: Thanks — do we have tenant id + example request?

maria_support: tenant=silverpine-prod, sample request included in ticket: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H \"Authorization: Bearer <KEY>\" -d '{\"model\":\"embed-compact-1\",\"input\":[\"doc text ... 8k chars ...\"]}'

raj_sre: I'll start digging into queues and RB metrics for that tenant. Any recent deploys to inference runtime? ops-bot: deploy-bot reports a runtime patch at 05:45 UTC to kernel scheduler.

raj_sre: Correlating — I see an increase in tail latency on the embed worker pool in us-west-2 from 05:50. p95 bumped from 420ms->900ms, p99 to ~2.7s. Concurrent tokens spiked for that tenant from 8->45 around 05:55.

maria_support: Silverpine says traffic pattern unchanged, mostly single-document embeds at ~1rps. Could this be noisy neighbor?

raj_sre: Possible. Looking at per-tenant circuit stats: their token bucket shows several rejection/backpressure events at 05:56. But interestingly the node where their requests landed has a high background batch size for other tenants — KV cache miss rate rose too.

emma_cs: Do we have traces for a slow request? Any long scheduling wait?

raj_sre: Pulled a slow span (trace: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/0a1b2c). Key parts:

```
SCHED_WAIT 450ms
BATCH_QUEUE_WAIT 1.1s
KERNEL_EXEC 55ms
KV_REBUILD 950ms
```

Note KV_REBUILD is suspicious — appears to be cache eviction/rehydration during a hot churn.

maria_support: Silverpine shared request IDs: r-00045f, r-00046a. Attached to ticket.

emma_cs: If KV cache churn is the issue, we can mitigate two ways: 1) temporary per-tenant allowlist/reservation to pin their requests to a pool with warmed caches, or 2) fallback model variant with smaller KV working set (embed-compact-1 -> embed-compact-1-quant). Which is faster?

raj_sre: Short term fastest: add them to the reservation allowlist so their requests go to reserved pool with warmed caches. That avoids widespread cache misses. I'll coordinate ops change. Need tenant id and time window.

maria_support: Confirmed tenant id: tenant:silverpine-prod. They request emergency mitigation for next 6 hours.

raj_sre: Doing the allowlist change now. Pushing reservation for tenant:silverpine-prod -> pool-embeds-resv-02, migration routing TTL 30s so in-flight not impacted.

ops-bot: action: reservation.apply user=raj_sre tenant=tenant:silverpine-prod pool=pool-embeds-resv-02 window=6h id=chg-98765 status=ok

raj_sre: Change applied. Can someone ask Silverpine to validate?

maria_support: pinging Silverpine — please run a couple of sample requests and report p99.

(10m later) maria_support: Silverpine confirmed p99 down to ~420ms and error rate normal. They reported no further spikes in the last 12 minutes. :white_check_mark:

emma_cs: Nice. Next steps:
- keep reservation for 6h, monitor KV cache hit ratio and batch sizes.
- run root cause: correlate kernel scheduler patch + eviction thresholds that aligned with workload churn.
- propose long-term: dynamic per-tenant cache pinning for high-SLA customers or adaptive eviction thresholds.

raj_sre: Collected data for postmortem: node IDs, traces, eviction logs attached to incident ticket INC-2026-498. I'll follow up with a config rollback experiment if we can reproduce in staging.

maria_support: I'll notify Silverpine of the follow-up plan and offer a rate override/reservation if they anticipate heavier windows.

emma_cs: Great. Closing slack loop. If any regression after reservation expires, re-open thread. :thumbsup:
